description: Markov-trace assembly chain for the proton on the CANONICAL 11-letter element: convention-D Wedderburn weights + seminormal characters + the finite-Jones axiom, giving tr_M(p, q_0) ≈ 0.6293284022. Written 2026-09-13 (bean qou-nhkv) to replace an ORPHAN artifact whose only builder was deprecated and which had been left in the grouped-era frame while its neutron and deuteron siblings moved to canonical. Unlike those siblings this chain has NO legacy-convention frontier: its character steps are computed on the canonical element rather than on a 5-letter stand-in. The leaf is read from canonical_trm_reference, not hardcoded.

steps.name: Partitions of 3 — Schur–Weyl basis at A=1
steps.operation: By Schur–Weyl duality the A=1 ambient Hecke algebra is H_3(q); partitions of 3 are (3), (2,1), (1,1,1). Same basis as the neutron and deuteron assemblies.

steps.name: Convention-D Wedderburn weights y_λ(q) at H_3
steps.operation: y_λ(q) from `markov_weights_symbolic.solve_y_lambda(3)`, the ladder linear system A y = b with A_{ij} = χ^{λ_j}(σ_1⋯σ_{i-1}) and b_i = z^i, z = q³/(q²+1) — convention D, owner ruling 2026-08-09. Under D the three-row weight VANISHES: y_(1,1,1) = 0, which is the level r = 2 row cap (bean qou-fq0f). The sign-rep character therefore cannot affect this assembly at all.

steps.name: Atomic-braid recipe for the proton — chain reference
steps.operation: Reference `atomic-braid-recipe-p-canonical.derivation.json`: the canonical proton element is 11 letters {σ: 6, σ⁻¹: 3, averaged: 2}, from quark content (u, u, d) + B₃ confinement + the borromean intra-nucleon core (σ₀σ₁⁻¹)³ made canonical by the 2026-09-05 owner ruling, bean `qou-hu1f`. TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES AGREE on this word: the recipe chain, and `trm_proton_five_values_census`, which records canonical_word_for(1,0) = [[1,1]x4, [0,1], [1,1]x2, [-1,2]x3, [0,2]] — the same breakdown by a different route. NOTE THE CONTRAST WITH THE SIBLING CHAINS: their steps 5–7 use a legacy 5-letter σ-word and their symbolic intermediate is illustrative-only. This chain does not do that; the character steps below are computed on the canonical element itself.
steps.output_value: T_w_p = canonical element, 11 letters {σ: 6, σ⁻¹: 3, averaged: 2}
steps.notes: Derivation chain: atomic-braid-recipe-p-canonical.derivation.json (builder: build_atomic_braid_recipe_canonical_chain.py). TERMINOLOGY: the 11 are LETTERS, not crossings — the object is a product of Hecke elements c·σ_g + d·1 and atom_braid_word_3A's docstring forbids reading a topological quantity off it.

steps.name: Characters χ^λ_q(T_w_p) on the canonical element
steps.operation: χ^λ as the trace of the seminormal matrix product for the canonical element, each letter (c, d, g) acting as c·ρ_λ(σ_g) + d·1 — `markov_weights_symbolic.chi_lambda_symbolic`. This is the route `atom_braid_word_3A`'s docstring names as the only valid one, and it applies the averaged-letter factor that the sibling chains' legacy steps omit. Exact over Q(q); no float64 anywhere.
steps.output_value: symbolic Laurent polynomials in q, one per λ ⊢ 3

steps.name: Finite-Jones assembly tr_M(p) = Σ_λ y_λ χ^λ
steps.operation: The Ocneanu/Jones–Markov trace as the y-weighted character sum, `markov_weights_symbolic.tr_M_canonical(crossings, 3)`. With y_(1,1,1) = 0 under convention D the sum runs over (3) and (2,1) only.

steps.name: Evaluate tr_M(p, q_0) at the proton pin
steps.operation: Substitute q := q_0 into the symbolic assembly. The value is READ from `canonical_trm_reference.tr_m_nucleon('proton')` rather than restated, so it cannot drift from its witness, and that accessor refuses a witness in the wrong or an undeclared intra-nucleon ordering (bean `qou-y4gi`).
steps.notes: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED: assembly_chain_11_letter_recompute_probe evaluates the same canonical element by the same seminormal route and obtains 0.62932840220292191817 at the proton pin. That probe predates this chain and shares no code path with the witness this leaf reads.
